preflop.definition: The first betting round: players hold two cards and there is no board yet.

flop.definition: The first three community cards and the betting round after them.

river.definition: The fifth and last community card.

board.definition: The community cards in the middle that every player uses.

blinds.definition: Forced bets posted by the small blind (SB) and big blind (BB) before the deal.

ante.definition: A small forced bet from every player before the deal.

button.definition: The dealer seat; it acts last after the flop.

position.definition: Your seat relative to the button. "In position" means acting after your opponent.

stack.definition: A player's chips. The effective stack is the smallest stack among the players in the pot.

pot.definition: All the chips bet in a hand.

side-pot.definition: A separate pot for players who bet more than an all-in player.

split.definition: A pot shared between equal hands.

showdown.definition: Showing the cards after the last betting round.

kicker.definition: A card outside the made hand that decides between equal hands.

nuts.definition: The best possible hand on a given board.

set.definition: Three of a kind made with a pocket pair and one board card.

trips.definition: Three of a kind made with one hole card and a pair on the board.

fold.definition: Give up your cards and leave the hand.

check.definition: Pass when nobody has bet on the street yet.

limp.definition: Enter the pot first by just calling the big blind.

open-raise.definition: The first raise of the hand after everyone before you folded (RFI).

iso-raise.definition: A raise over a limper to play heads-up against them.

squeeze.definition: A 3-bet after an open-raise and a call.

steal.definition: A raise from a late seat to win the blinds.

range.definition: All the hands a player can hold in a spot.

combo.definition: One specific two-card hand; there are 1326 of them.

suited.definition: Two cards of the same suit (s in notation: AKs).

offsuit.definition: Two cards of different suits (o in notation: AKo).

domination.definition: When your opponent shares your high card with a better kicker: AQ against AK.

outs.definition: Cards that will most likely make your hand the best.

draw.definition: A hand one card short of a straight or flush.

gutshot.definition: A straight draw missing a middle card: 4 outs.

pot-odds.definition: The price of a call compared with the pot: the equity a call needs to pay off.

equity.definition: The share of the pot a hand wins on average.

ev.definition: Expected value: what a decision wins on average.

implied-odds.definition: Future winnings after your hand comes in.

blocker.definition: A card you hold that reduces the combos of a hand your opponent can have.

variance.definition: The swing of results around the expected value: luck in the short run.

c-bet.definition: A flop bet by the player who raised before the flop.

value-bet.definition: A bet made to be called by worse hands.

bluff.definition: A bet with a weak hand to make a better hand fold.

semi-bluff.definition: A bluff with a hand that has outs.

check-raise.definition: Check first, then raise your opponent's bet.

tilt.definition: Playing on emotion after bad luck, usually worse than normal.

bankroll.definition: The chips or money set aside for playing. In this app, only play chips.
